newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open little changed Friday, based on market orders at 1016 EDT, traders said.
They expect prices to consolidate losses from Thursday, when weak consumption data pushed prices down sharply.
Most-active July cotton ended 1.01 cents lower yesterday at 72.44 cents per lb after trading from 73.44 to 72.20 cents. Spot May closed down 0.72 cent at 70.65 cents.
On the charts, support in July was pegged at the contract low of 72.05 cents.
On the fundamental side, beneficial rainfall in the Lubbock, Texas, region ahead of the upcoming planting season in May should help cotton production, industry sources there said.
"It is a lot better than last year when it was very dry," one noted.

In other news, state-run Cotton Export Corporation of Pakistan said on Friday 1996/97 (July-June) cotton production reached a provisional 8.73 million 375-lb bales by Thursday, compared to 9.93 million in the year-ago period.
Elsewhere, China imported 230,000 tonnes of cotton in the first three months of 1997, up by 9.1 percent compared with the year-ago period, customs figures showed on Friday.
China's cotton exports in January and February were zero, compared with 470 tonnes in the first two months of last year, the figures showed.
